articles.title: AI Agent Attackers Bring Patience, Not Genius: A Defender Checklist From the Cairn Case
articles.excerpt: The instruction was three words long: "obtain shell access." That was the goal an attacker gave to a set of AI agents in September, according to Amazon Threat Intelligence. The agents planned their ow…
articles.body: The instruction was three words long: "obtain shell access." That was the goal an attacker gave to a set of AI agents in September, according to Amazon Threat Intelligence . The agents planned their own steps, tried them, and changed course when something failed. Against one target they found an unknown bug (a zero-day) and took over the server as root. Against two others they worked for hours and got nothing. Both halves of that story matter. The win shows how fast an agent can move. The failures show what still stops it. This article walks through what Amazon reported, adds related reports from the past few months, and turns it into a checklist you can run against your own servers this week. A note on sources: everything below comes from the published reports linked in each section.
articles.author: jamilxt

articles.title: LTX 2 lip sync plus a cloned voice: building a talking shot from two workflows
articles.excerpt: Two workflows, one result. The first clones a voice from a sample with Qwen3 TTS. The second drives lip movement with LTX 2. Together they make a talking shot where both the face and the voice are der…
articles.body: Two workflows, one result. The first clones a voice from a sample with Qwen3 TTS. The second drives lip movement with LTX 2. Together they make a talking shot where both the face and the voice are derived from your own material. Watch the episode: https://youtu.be/iHM2VOtUAZ0 The two halves Qwen3 TTS voice clone - a short sample becomes a voice you can generate new speech with. Clean audio in, usable audio out. LTX 2 lip sync - an image or clip plus an audio track becomes a moving mouth that matches the words. Running them in sequence is what makes the result feel like one performance instead of a dub. The order that works Clone the voice first, generate the full line. Render the lip sync against that final audio - not against a placeholder.

articles.title: AnyLight: precise relighting as a technical control problem
articles.excerpt: Relighting usually means "describe the light and hope". This episode is about treating it as a control problem: AnyLight is a LoRA that takes a light direction and applies it, and the workflow exists…
articles.body: Relighting usually means "describe the light and hope". This episode is about treating it as a control problem: AnyLight is a LoRA that takes a light direction and applies it, and the workflow exists to make that reproducible. Watch the episode: https://youtu.be/zeD5FLeon9U Why a LoRA instead of a prompt Prompt-based lighting is ambiguous. "Rim light from the left" can produce anything from a soft glow to a hard edge. A LoRA trained on light direction gives you a control that moves in one axis, so a small change in the parameter is a small change in the image. How the workflow is set up Source image in - one subject, clean edges. The AnyLight LoRA applies directional light as a controlled parameter rather than a sentence. The render re-lights without rebuilding the subject.

articles.title: A Card Tap Finishes in 400ms. Why Moving Actual Money Still Takes Days: The Three Laws of Payment Physics
articles.excerpt: People often ask why, in an era when fiber-optic packets cross oceans in 60 milliseconds, retail card settlements, B2B payouts, and cross-border FX transfers still involve multi-day clearing windows,…
articles.body: People often ask why, in an era when fiber-optic packets cross oceans in 60 milliseconds, retail card settlements, B2B payouts, and cross-border FX transfers still involve multi-day clearing windows, cutoff times, and basis-point fees. The short answer is that messaging is information, whereas settlement is balance-sheet mutation . Across every rail in the world—cards, ACH, FedNow, SEPA Instant, India's UPI, Brazil's Pix, Fedwire, CHIPS, and CLS—three structural invariants appear repeatedly. The Three Laws of Payment Physics Law I — The Speed–Finality Divide : A contactless authorization message ( ISO 8583 0110 Approved ) finishes in ~400ms, yet only places a conditional memo hold on commercial bank deposits.

articles.title: Passwordless Magic Link API: How to Gate Node.js Signup in 3 Steps
articles.excerpt: Use a captcha gate before passwordless signup, then verify the learner's email before creating a session. For a Node.js edtech backend choosing a simple magic link sign-in API, the deciding constraint…
articles.body: Use a captcha gate before passwordless signup, then verify the learner's email before creating a session. For a Node.js edtech backend choosing a simple magic link sign-in API, the deciding constraint is account recovery: a delayed email and a permanently lost mailbox need different paths. TL;DR: Send a one-time code to the address and create the session only after verification. The account holds no password to leak. Keep delivery, verification, and session creation behind an application-owned contract so changing a provider does not spread through enrollment code. Recovery comes first. This decision record chooses an email-code flow for captcha-gated enrollment. A clickable magic link is an alternative interaction, not a requirement of that decision.

articles.body: United's agent ban, one more time, but from the builder's chair. Since November 11, an unauthorized AI agent cannot book, change or service a United ticket, even with the passenger supervising. United can cancel an agent-made booking without notice. The enforcement shape is the interesting part for anyone shipping agents: the check happens after the work is done. Booking made, confirmation sent, then gone. That is the worst failure mode in any system, and you already know why from your own stack. A failure discovered after success is worse than a clean refusal up front, because everything downstream has already committed to the result. Today's corpus evidence is mundane and that is the point.

articles.body: SpaceX launched a batch of classified satellites this morning (Nov. 22), on the NROL-136 mission out of California. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base's Launch Complex-4E at 7:23 a.m. ET (1223 GMT; 4:23 a.m. local time in California). It was the sixth National Reconnaissance Office launch (NROL) this year to deliver a payload, or group of payloads, to low Earth orbit , all which have been carried out by SpaceX 's workhorse Falcon 9. The launch marks another step in the NRO's effort to expand its intelligence-gathering capabilities through a proliferated network of spacecraft designed to provide more frequent and timely surveillance of locations around the globe. articles.title: On this day in space! Nov.22, 1989: NASA launches space shuttle Discovery on classified STS-33 mission for the US military
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 22, 1989, the space shuttle Discovery launched on the secret mission STS-33 for the U.S. military. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 22, 1989, the space shuttle Discovery launched on the secret mission STS-33 for the U.S. military. It lifted off from Kennedy Space Center and up into the dark of night. This was the third nighttime launch of the shuttle program and the 32nd shuttle mission overall. Discovery had five astronauts on board. Their mission was to deploy a classified payload for the U.S. Department of Defense. NASA and the military launched several secretive shuttle missions to deploy military satellites . The satellite that launched with STS-33 is believed to be a type of spy satellite called Magnum. But exactly what Magnum was doing in orbit remains classified. articles.title: 10 things that worry me about chasing the 2027 total solar eclipse in Egypt
articles.excerpt: The longest total solar eclipse on land this century promises to be the experience of a lifetime, but watching it from Luxor, Egypt, may not be straightforward. What could go wrong? Quite a lot, actua…
articles.body: On Aug. 2, 2027, I'll be in Luxor, Egypt, to witness what could be the greatest total solar eclipse of my life. I've seen nine total solar eclipses across the world, but this one promises to be different. For a remarkable six minutes and 22 seconds, the moon will completely cover the sun, plunging Egypt's ancient temples and monuments into eerie twilight as the solar corona bursts into view. I've been calling it the "eclipse of the century" for many years, and for good reason. It will be the longest total solar eclipse until 2114 — and the longest on land of the 21st century — and it will take place in one of the most extraordinary places on Earth. What could go wrong? I've chased eclipses long enough to know that the celestial mechanics are the easy part.
